item.text: The relocation path ranks candidate documents from shingle hits and then aligns text within a bounded window. I’m checking cases where that ranking or window can pick the wrong span or leave a valid anchor stale.

type doc_contents = Active of string | Deleted

module Documents = struct
  let create_table db =
    U.exec db
      {|
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "documents" (
          doc_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
          source_kind  TEXT    NOT NULL,
          source_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
          locator      TEXT    NOT NULL,
          revision     INTEGER NOT NULL,
          content_hash TEXT,
          contents     BLOB,
          UNIQUE (source_kind, source_name, locator)
        )
      |}

  let param_of_contents = function
    | Active c -> U.Nullable_blob (Some c)
    | Deleted -> U.Nullable_blob None

                                                                          
                                                         
  let col_doc_id = 0
  let col_source_kind = 1
  let col_source_name = 2
  let col_locator = 3
  let col_revision = 4
  let col_content_hash = 5
  let col_contents = 6

  let content_hash_of_contents = function
    | Active c -> Some (Digest.to_hex (Digest.string c))
    | Deleted -> None

  let source_params (source : T.source) locator =
    let source_kind, source_name = columns_of_source source in
    [
      U.Text (Util.Text.validate_exn source_kind);
      U.Text (Util.Text.validate_exn source_name);
      U.Text (Util.Text.validate_exn locator);
    ]

  let create db ~(source : T.source) ~locator ~(contents : doc_contents) :
      T.doc_id =
    exec_returning_one db
      {|INSERT INTO "documents"
          (source_kind, source_name, locator, revision, content_hash, contents)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, 0, ?, ?)
        RETURNING doc_id|}
      (source_params source locator
      @ [
          U.Nullable_text
            (Option.map Util.Text.validate_exn
               (content_hash_of_contents contents));
          param_of_contents contents;
        ])
      ~f:(fun stmt -> A.Doc_id.of_int64_exn (Sqlite3.column_int64 stmt 0))

  let create_or_update db ~(source : T.source) ~locator
      ~(contents : doc_contents) : T.doc_id =
    exec_returning_one db
      {|INSERT INTO "documents"
          (source_kind, source_name, locator, revision, content_hash, contents)
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, 0, ?, ?)
        ON CONFLICT (source_kind, source_name, locator) DO UPDATE
          SET revision =
                CASE
                  WHEN content_hash IS NOT excluded.content_hash
                  THEN revision + 1
                  ELSE revision
                END,
              content_hash = excluded.content_hash,
              contents = excluded.contents
        RETURNING doc_id|}
      (source_params source locator
      @ [
          U.Nullable_text
            (Option.map Util.Text.validate_exn
               (content_hash_of_contents contents));
          param_of_contents contents;
        ])
      ~f:(fun stmt -> A.Doc_id.of_int64_exn (Sqlite3.column_int64 stmt 0))

  let row_to_doc_meta stmt : T.doc_meta =
    {
      doc_id = A.Doc_id.of_int64_exn (Sqlite3.column_int64 stmt col_doc_id);
      source_doc =
        {
          source =
            source_of_columns
              ( Sqlite3.column_text stmt col_source_kind,
                Sqlite3.column_text stmt col_source_name );
          locator = Sqlite3.column_text stmt col_locator;
        };
      revision = Int64.to_int (Sqlite3.column_int64 stmt col_revision);
      content_hash =
        Sqlite3.column stmt col_content_hash |> Sqlite3.Data.to_string;
    }

  let get_by_id db (doc_id : T.doc_id) : T.doc_meta option =
    U.query_rows db
      {|SELECT doc_id, source_kind, source_name, locator, revision, content_hash
        FROM "documents" WHERE doc_id = ?|}
      [ U.Int64 (A.Doc_id.to_int64 doc_id) ]
      ~f:row_to_doc_meta
    |> function
    | [] -> None
    | x :: _ -> Some x

  let get_by_locator db ~(source : T.source) locator : T.doc_meta option =
    U.query_rows db
      {|SELECT doc_id, source_kind, source_name, locator, revision, content_hash
        FROM "documents"
        WHERE source_kind = ? AND source_name = ? AND locator = ?|}
      (source_params source locator)
      ~f:row_to_doc_meta
    |> function
    | [] -> None
    | x :: _ -> Some x
                | Text.Up_to_date _ ->
                    fail
                      "this heuristic isn't expected to survive edits this \
                       densely scattered -- if it now does, that's an \
                       improvement worth re-documenting here, not a bug"
                | Text.Outdated -> ())));
    Testo.create ~category:cat
      "FALSE POSITIVE (known limitation): an anchor whose own text was \
       replaced can relocate onto an unrelated document that happens to \
       share a long verbatim block with the original" (fun () ->
        let boilerplate = String.sub big_text 0 64 in
        let files =
          make_files
            [
              ("a.ml", "header_a " ^ boilerplate ^ " footer_a");
              ("b.ml", "unrelated_prefix " ^ boilerplate ^ " unrelated_suffix");
            ]
        in
        with_declared_test_db files (fun store ->
            ignore
              (snd
                 (Text.add_file store (source_doc "a.ml")
                    (source files "a.ml"))
                : Text.anchor list);
            ignore
              (snd
                 (Text.add_file store (source_doc "b.ml")
                    (source files "b.ml"))
                : Text.anchor list);
            let start = String.length "header_a " in
            let anchor =
              Text.add_anchor store (source_doc "a.ml") (source files "a.ml")
                ~expected_revision:0 ~start
                ~end_:(start + String.length boilerplate)
            in
                                                                           
                                                                    
                                                                        
                         
            Hashtbl.replace files "a.ml"
              "completely different content now, nothing like before at all, \
               not even close";
            let _, changed =
              Text.add_file store (source_doc "a.ml") (source files "a.ml")
            in
            match find_by_id changed anchor.anchor_id with
            | None -> fail "expected the anchor to be reported as changed"
            | Some a ->
                Testo.check
                  ~msg:
                    "relocates onto b.ml's unrelated copy of the shared \
                     boilerplate, even though a.ml's actual edit has nothing \
                     to do with b.ml -- pure text matching can't tell the \
                     difference"
                  Testo.string "b.ml" a.source_doc.locator));
    Testo.create ~category:cat
      "content_hash and revision both stay the same across a no-op re-index, \
       and both change when the content actually changes" (fun () ->
        let files = make_files [ ("a.ml", "first content") ] in
        with_declared_test_db files (fun store ->

I found three potential issues in anchor relocation:

- **P0 — An unchanged anchor can move to the wrong document.** Candidates with equal coverage and hit counts are ordered by document ID, with no preference for the anchor’s current document. If an older indexed document contains the same text, editing unrelated text in the anchor’s document can silently move the anchor there. [Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:348)

- **P1 — Relocation depends on when the destination is indexed.** If the original document is deleted before its replacement is indexed, the failed attempt is recorded against the original document’s revision. Indexing the replacement later only retries anchors attached to that replacement, so the old anchor stays outdated until the original document changes again. [Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:491), [DB.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/DB.ml:852)

- **P1 — Repeated text can leave an intact anchor outdated.** Shingle indexing drops every occurrence of a shingle that repeats within a document. An anchor in repeated text may therefore have no hits in its own document; an unrelated edit triggers relocation, but the unchanged text cannot be found. [Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:151)
